title: Approximate percentiles

import * as C from "@constants";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";
import TestPlan from "@components/TestPlan.astro";

This walkthrough uses a `response_times` table to show approximate percentiles end to end. {C.TIMESCALE_DB} implements them with bounded-memory sketches instead of sorting every value, which keeps latency predictable on large datasets and {C.CAGG}s.

By default, {C.TOOLKIT_LONG} uses `uddsketch`, but you can also choose
`tdigest`. For algorithm trade-offs, see [advanced aggregation methods](/build/data-management/hyperfunctions/percentile-approx/advanced-agg).

## Run an approximate percentage query

In this procedure, we use an example table called `response_times` that contains
information about how long a server takes to respond to API calls.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Create a ${C.CAGG} for daily aggregates`}>
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW response_times_daily
WITH (timescaledb.continuous)
AS SELECT
  time_bucket('1 day'::interval, ts) as bucket,
  percentile_agg(response_time_ms)
FROM response_times
GROUP BY 1;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Query the ninety-fifth percentile over the last 30 days">
Re-aggregate the aggregate to get the last 30 days:

```sql
SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, rollup(percentile_agg)) as threshold
FROM response_times_daily
WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval);
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create an alert">
```sql
WITH t as (SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, rollup(percentile_agg)) as threshold
FROM response_times_daily
WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval))

SELECT count(*)
FROM response_times
WHERE ts > now()- '1 minute'::interval
AND response_time_ms > (SELECT threshold FROM t);
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

For more information about percentile approximation API calls, see the
[hyperfunction API documentation](/reference/toolkit/percentile-approximation/uddsketch/percentile_agg).

<TestPlan>
target: cloud, self-hosted

1. fork the service
2. [cloud] select the service
3. [self-hosted] run command: `echo 'APT::Get::Assume-Yes "true";' > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/90doctest`
4. [self-hosted] run command: `apt update`
5. [self-hosted] run command: `apt install timescaledb-toolkit-postgresql-18`
6. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;`
7. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb_toolkit;`
8. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE response_times (ts TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, endpoint TEXT, response_time_ms DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.partition_column = 'ts');`
9. run SQL: `INSERT INTO response_times SELECT now() - (g || ' minutes')::interval, '/api', 100 + (g % 100) * 9 FROM generate_series(2, 20000) AS g;`
10. run SQL: `INSERT INTO response_times VALUES (now() - INTERVAL '20 seconds', '/api', 5000);`
11. run SQL: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW response_times_daily WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS SELECT time_bucket('1 day'::interval, ts) as bucket, percentile_agg(response_time_ms) FROM response_times GROUP BY 1;`
12. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.continuous_aggregates WHERE view_name = 'response_times_daily'`
13. run SQL: `SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, rollup(percentile_agg)) as threshold FROM response_times_daily WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval);`
14. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, rollup(percentile_agg)) AS threshold FROM response_times_daily WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval)) t WHERE threshold BETWEEN 900 AND 1000`
15. run SQL: `WITH t as (SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, rollup(percentile_agg)) as threshold FROM response_times_daily WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval)) SELECT count(*) FROM response_times WHERE ts > now()- '1 minute'::interval AND response_time_ms > (SELECT threshold FROM t);`
16. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM response_times WHERE ts > now() - '10 minutes'::interval AND response_time_ms > (SELECT approx_percentile(0.95, rollup(percentile_agg)) FROM response_times_daily WHERE bucket >= time_bucket('1 day'::interval, now() - '30 days'::interval)) HAVING count(*) = 1`
</TestPlan>
